title: Huron on I-5: Exit 325, Jayne Avenue, Services
meta: Huron, California sits east of I-5 at exit 325 (Jayne Avenue). See nearby gas, rest areas and landmarks along this stretch of Fresno County farmland.
intro: Huron is a farm town of about 6,200 people east of I-5 at exit 325, Jayne Avenue. It began in 1888 as a Southern Pacific water stop and swells to more than 15,000 at harvest time. The freeway here crosses the West Side farmland of Fresno County.

faq.q: What exit is Huron on I-5?
faq.a: Huron is at exit 325, Jayne Avenue, and the town lies east of the freeway.

faq.q: Is there gas at the Huron exit on I-5?
faq.a: Gas is mapped at exit 325 in OpenStreetMap data: three stations, with Shell and Valero among the brands listed. This is as mapped, not live, so it does not show whether any are open.

faq.q: Where is the nearest rest area to Huron on I-5?
faq.a: The Coalinga-Avenal Rest Area at mile 320.2 is about 4.8 miles south of Huron and serves both directions. Going north, the John "Chuck" Erreca Rest Area at mile 385.9 is about 60.9 miles ahead and also serves both directions.
Huron has about 6,200 people, rising to more than 15,000 at harvest time when migrant farmworkers arrive. It began in 1888 as a water stop on the Southern Pacific Railroad.

faq.q: What is the big electrical yard near Huron on I-5?
faq.a: It is Gates Substation, on the right going north around mile 324. It is a key junction on the power lines linking Northern and Southern California.
